title: Terraform steward module for private EKS control plane bootstrapping & health orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood Private needs a single, well-documented Terraform module and companion operational playbook that reliably bootstraps EKS control planes inside customer VPCs and provides automated health orchestration during upgrades and day-2 operations. Existing modules are fragmented across repos and lack consistent preflight checks, immutable bootstrap paths, and observable health gates.

Goal:
Deliver a production-ready Terraform module (and a playbook) that: 1) performs idempotent, immutable bootstraps of EKS control plane resources; 2) embeds preflight and postflight health probes; 3) provides safe upgrade hooks and canary gates (Terraform + Hooks); and 4) integrates with Redwood's KMS + audit logging and the Console monitoring dashboards.

Scope and constraints:
- Module must be self-contained (VPC subnets, SGs referenced, role bindings) but not re-create customer-managed networks.
- Allow declarative variant selection (managed EKS vs self-managed control plane abstraction for air-gapped installs).
- Must not break existing private clusters; provide migration path and backwards-compatible input flags.
- No runtime agents installed by default; health checks use AWS APIs (EKSA / EKS controlplane status), CloudWatch metrics, and optional agent-backed probes for deeper state.

Design highlights:
- Inputs: vpc_id, subnet_ids (control plane), control_plane_name, kms_key_arn, admin_users, signed_manifest_url (optional), bootstrap_mode: [immutable, in-place], upgrade_window, canary_percentage.
- Outputs: control_plane_id, bootstrap_manifest_hash, last_applied_time, health_sentinel_arn.
- Preflight validations: subnet reachability, KMS key access, certificate signing config, IAM role trust boundaries, terraform input schema validation.
- Health orchestration: a lightweight Lambda-based probe (owned by the module) that performs periodic checks and emits telemetry to CloudWatch/Datadog; Terraform creates a CloudWatch alarm and SLO dashboard links. Operator can opt out.
- Upgrade guard: stageable rollout via canary percentage and an automated rollback hook that creates a shadow change and stalls plan/apply until health gates pass.
- Drift detection: scheduled job that compares bootstrap_manifest_hash with live cluster state and files tickets via webhook (configurable).

Migration and compatibility:
- Provide a migration sub-command and example workflow in the playbook to move from old modules to this steward module with minimal downtime.
- Add feature flag input preserve_old_resources to allow staged cutover.

Acceptance criteria:
- Module provisions an EKS control plane in a test VPC end-to-end with immutable bootstrap mode and produces deterministic outputs.
- Preflight failure cases are surfaced as clear Terraform diagnostics and prevent apply.
- Canary upgrade path can advance 0% -> 50% -> 100% with automated health checks between stages and a documented rollback.
- Monitoring: Console dashboard link shows per-cluster control-plane latency, control-plane error rate, and last bootstrap hash; CloudWatch alarms trigger on probe failures.
- Security: KMS encrypted secrets are used, IAM least-privilege roles are created and audited.

Out of scope:
- Worker node autoscaling and workload-level observability (handled by node/deployment modules).
- Full on-prem air-gapped artifact distribution (only manifest signing + signed_manifest_url support).
acceptance_criteria: Idempotent immutable bootstrap completes with same outputs on repeated apply
Preflight checks block invalid inputs and surface clear errors
Canary upgrade flow enforces health gates and supports safe rollback
Module integrates with KMS and emits health sentinel metric to CloudWatch
testing_plan: unit: terraform plan diff tests (tfsec + checkov) in CI
integration: provisioning against a constrained test VPC (ephemeral) with simulated failures
chaos: inject control plane API latency and verify canary rollback triggers
e2e: full provisioning -> canary upgrade -> rollback -> migration from legacy module
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Module merged behind feature flag and used by internal staging clusters
Stage 2: Enable for low-risk customer pilot clusters (1-2 customers)
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to all private clusters with migration support and a 2-week monitoring window
